MINUTES
  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MARCH 15, 2022

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

An adjourned meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 12:18 p.m. on the Council Chambers Patio, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
MAYOR ZERUNYAN.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Pledge of Allegiance led by MAYOR ZERUNYAN.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson
  Associate Planner Dean Flores

4.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  DRAFT GENERAL PLAN 2040 WORKSHOP: DISCUSSION OF LAND USE
  ELEMENT, MOBILITY ELEMENT AND HOUSING ELEMENT

MAYOR ZERUNYAN provided a brief introduction regarding the topics to be discussed
during the workshop.

City Manager Grammer introduced consultants John Bellas and Surabhi Barbhaya of
Michael Baker International, and traffic consultant John Muggeridge of Fehr and Peers.

Consultant Bellas explained that the purpose of the workshop was to discuss and seek
consensus from the City Council on the following portions of the General Plan Update: Land
Use Element, Mobility Element and Housing Element. He began by revisiting the Vision
Statement at the beginning of the document, and presented the updated “Guiding
Principles.”

Consultant Bellas noted that the focus of the meeting would be the changes made to the
various Elements. He explained that the City has a good General Plan in place, and the goal
is to update the Plan and adjust it to what is envisioned for the next 20 years.

Community Development and Public Works Director Wahba introduced and summarized the
Land Use Element, including the purpose, goals, policies and implementation measures.
He introduced a discussion about the Academy Center Office Complex, noting that adding
a “Mixed-Use Overlay” designation to “Commercial Office” was being considered, in an
attempt to add more residential building opportunities.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN expressed his concern about current traffic at Academy
Hill, stating that a queuing analysis was needed.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
MARCH 15, 2022
 Director Wahba noted that approximately 90% of the land area of the City in this General
Plan Update remains unchanged.

Discussion ensued regarding the Academy Center Office Complex and the significant traffic
concerns if the area were allowed to be built for residential, discretionary approval and future
General Plan amendments.

It was the consensus of the Council to not change the designation of the Academy Center
Office Complex.

Director Wahba then outlined the proposed designation of “Neighborhood Commercial” for
the Sea Horse Riding Club property that would allow for “Mixed Use Overlay” at 22
units/acre. Discussion ensued about the definition of the “Neighborhood Commercial”
designation, concerns about the perception of changing an equestrian facility in an
equestrian community, and the existing nuisances of smell and dust from the stables that
could negatively affect any future residential development.

It was the consensus of the Council to not change the designation of the Sea Horse Riding
Club.

Director Wahba next outlined the proposed designation of “Neighborhood Commercial” for
the Rolling Hills Business Park property that would allow for “Mixed Use Overlay” at 22
units/acre. Discussion ensued about the many positive aspects about this location for
potential residential units.

It was the consensus of the Council to change the designation of Rolling Hills Business Park
to “Neighborhood Commercial.”

Director Wahba next outlined the proposed designation of “Neighborhood Commercial” for
Kelly’s Corner/General Store that would allow for “Mixed Use Overlay” at 22 units/acre.
Discussion ensued about the “Landmark Overlay Zone” designation and the protection of
the General Store as a historical building if residential units were built adjacent to it on the
property.

Consultant Bellas suggested adding into the Plan that any new buildings at this location
would need to be designed and developed in accordance with the Secretary of the Interior’s
Standards for historic preservation.

It was the consensus of the Council to change the designation of the Kelly’s Corner/General
Store property to “Neighborhood Commercial.”

Director Wahba next outlined opportunities for Workforce Housing on the following
institutional properties: Dapplegray Elementary, Palos Verdes Peninsula High School and
Rolling Hills Covenant Church.

Discussion ensued about the process of establishing Workforce Housing on a property,
affordability planning for first year teachers, and access to both school properties.
Discussion continued regarding the potential for the Rolling Hills Covenant Church property,
and it’s parking challenges.

It was the consensus of the Council to limit Dapplegray Elementary and Palos Verdes
Peninsula High School to Workforce Housing, and Rolling Hills Covenant Church to
Workforce Housing and other types of affordable housing.

Planning Manager Naughton discussed the following for the Commercial District Mixed Use
Overlay District in the Land Use / Mobility Element: Vision and guiding principles, market
study – proforma analysis, parking study, RHNA requirements, General Plan Advisory
Committee workshop and survey, recent developments, age of structures and use of vision
plan as a guide.

Discussion ensued about the Vision Study map and the acres designated for the Peninsula
Center, and the opportunities outlined envisioning what a build-out scenario might look like

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MARCH 15, 2022
 for the Commercial District. Planning Manager Naughton noted that incentives can be
tailored specifically to the various community benefits from specific properties.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN noted an error on page 114 of Appendix A, which should
be 30 units/acre, not 22 units/acre as listed.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN also noted on page 146 of Appendix A, the grand total
does not include the commercial section value, which should be corrected.

Planning Manager Naughton summarized the proposed changes to the Commercial District
Mixed Use Overlay District in the Land Use / Mobility Element.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN expressed concern about the green space designated
in the Peninsula Center that would potentially replace vital parking spaces. Discussion
ensued about the need for parking in the Peninsula Center versus the need for a safe
gathering space. Consultant Bellas proposed the option of making a space in the Peninsula
Center with permeable pavers that would be capable of having vehicles drive over or park
on them during portions of the day, and can roped off for a farmers market or recreational
activity.

It was the consensus of the Council to design and footnote this space as a flex space as
discussed.

Discussion ensued about proposed changes to Bart Earle Way.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN called for a recess at 2:09 pm.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN reconvened the meeting at 2:25 pm.

Planning Manager Naughton summarized the Commercial District Vision Plan, and the
proposed changes to Bart Earle Way that include incentivizing business owners by offering
to give them more land in the hopes of bringing in more meaningful development.
Discussion ensued about the desire and various ways to make Bart Earle Way more
pedestrian friendly, and the creation of a two-sided more walkable commercial area.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN suggested leaving the buildings on Bart Earle Way in their current
locations, while creating a pedestrian walkway from Drybank Drive to Beechgate Drive.
Discussion ensued about reducing the width of Silver Spur Road and/or Bart Earle Way, and
creating a promenade of outdoor dining.

It was the consensus of the Council to remove the current language in the proposed plan
about vacating Bart Earle Way, and include language to make it a more pedestrian-friendly
promenade area as an implementation measure as discussed.

Consultant Muggeridge discussed the capacity at the Silver Spur Road and Hawthorne
Boulevard intersection.

Planning Manager Naughton introduced and summarized the Mobility Element, including
the purpose, goals, policies and implementation measures.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN expressed concern regarding the parking study and the
suggestion of one parking space per unit rather than two.

Planning Manager Naughton introduced and summarized the Housing Element, including
the purpose, goals, policies and implementation measures.

It was the consensus of the Council to change the overall increase from 22 dwelling
units/acre to 30 dwelling units/acre in the Commercial District.

City Manager Grammer summarized the final steps for the General Plan Update, which
include bringing the General Plan Update and Final EIR back to the City Council on April 26,
2022 for a noticed public hearing, for final adoption.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MARCH 15, 2022
 6.  ADJOURNMENT

At 3:24 pm MAYOR ZERUNYAN adjourned the meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Frank V. Zerunyan
City Clerk  Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MARCH 15, 2022
